Results.ReviewText: I have always had a hard time with the Weber prices so I kept buying the cheaper units, until now.  I realized that over the last 10 years or so I've spent over $600-700 on three cheapos and considering the 10 year Weber warranty, I would have been ahead of the game buying a Weber years  ago.  I did however get quite a kick at how many individual parts I unpacked.  There were so many things not put together that I made a joke to my wife about, why Weber even bothered to put the pins in to connect the lid to the bottom of the grill.  Only to realize I think they were playing  a big joke, because with the lid being the only thing they assembled they later tell you to unassemble it in the assembly instructions.  All in all I still had it assembled fairly quickly by myself and I choose to skip the part about taking the lid off.  I just thought it was humorous.  So far our cooking experience has been really good and it looks like it's built to last.
Results.Title: Great grill and good price.

Results.ReviewText:
As an adult with a family of four, this is our first “real” grill that was more of an investment than a quick summer grilling solution. Great grill! Easy to assemble, like everything that one needs to assemble at home, use the correct screw driver head and use common sense when aligning and tightening it all down and it should go smoothly. I assembled this grill myself (33yr/M) in my living room while everyone was sleeping. When built, it’s quite sturdy. Or first meal on it was 3 1” NY strips and 1.25” porterhouse. We like well done beef in our household (sue me) and this grill performed flawlessly. Adequate and accurate even heating across the grilling grates that produced excellent hash marks. It holds heat well too. 16 minutes later we had steakhouse quality cuts grilled to perfection for 1/5 of the cost of going out. 

Worth every penny. The 3 burner model is a good size for a family of four plus a few guests. If you have lesser grilling needs, the 2 burner model would be a real nice consideration. Especially if it’s just one or two people with the occasional guest.

The Spirit line is indeed a basic grill. Side table and 2/3 burners. That’s it. But it’s such a nice grill. More “affordable” brands offer all the bells and whistles that much more expensive Weber’s offer but what you get is a season or two and things start to go out and you have to replace it. You may get less features with the Spirit’s, but what you get is quality. I look forward to using my Weber for years to come.
Results.Title: Great for a family of 4+

Results.ReviewText: This is the best gas grill I’ve owned. The construction of it seems very solid and durable. I’m hoping it’ll last 10-15 years with proper maintenance and cleaning. This grill heats up fast! It’s so easy to dial the temperature up and down for perfect even heating across all three burners. So far I’ve cooked chicken breasts, spare ribs and a ribeye. All of the meats have turned out beautifully seared on the outside and juicy on the inside! If you’re looking for a good quality gas grill, get the Weber Spirit II E-310!

45010001.Description:
Get ready to step up your grilling experience. As the family sits down for dinner, or a couple of friends come over for a bite – this three burner grill will do its magic. With the spacious cooking area you can sear steaks on one side while grilling an appetizer on the other, and the convenient open-cart allows you to keep your tools and equipment within reach. Armed with the strong GS4 grilling system, this gas grill is sure to take you and your meals to the next level.


 This product requires assembly.
